These tools will try to guess the key length of the cipher and determine the most probable key shift per key group. See \u003ca href=\"#heuristics\"\u003eHeuristics\u003c/a\u003e for more info.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eYou can call \u003ccode\u003eplayground.py\u003c/code\u003e and \u003ccode\u003esolver.py\u003c/code\u003e with command line arguments \u003ccode\u003e-v\u003c/code\u003e or \u003ccode\u003e-q\u003c/code\u003e (or both), to control the verbosity of the output (see \u003ca href=\"#l-log-levels\"\u003eLog levels\u003c/a\u003e).\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eLP pages and notation\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-lp-pages-and-notation\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: LP pages and notation\" href=\"#lp-pages-and-notation\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe \u003ccode\u003epages\u003c/code\u003e folder contains all LP pages in text and graphic. Note, I have double checked each and every rune while copying and added missing whitespace characters like \u003ccode\u003e'\u003c/code\u003e and \u003ccode\u003e\"\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eRune values are taken from Gematria, with these unicode characters representing: space (\u003ccode\u003e•\u003c/code\u003e), period (\u003ccode\u003e⁘\u003c/code\u003e), comma (\u003ccode\u003e⁚\u003c/code\u003e), semicolon (\u003ccode\u003e⁖\u003c/code\u003e), and chapter mark (\u003ccode\u003e⁜\u003c/code\u003e).\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe LP library\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-the-lp-library\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: The LP library\" href=\"#the-lp-library\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThese files you probably wont need to touch unless you want to modify some output behavior or rune handling. E.g. if you want to add a rune multiply method. These are the building blocks for the main components.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eutils.py\u003c/code\u003e, a small collection of reusable functions like \u003ccode\u003erev\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eis_prime\u003c/code\u003e, and \u003ccode\u003eis_emirp\u003c/code\u003e (reverse prime) checking.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eRuneText.py\u003c/code\u003e is the representation layer. The class \u003ccode\u003eRuneText\u003c/code\u003e holds an array of \u003ccode\u003eRune\u003c/code\u003e objects, which represent the individual runes. Each \u003ccode\u003eRune\u003c/code\u003e has the attributes \u003ccode\u003erune\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003etext\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eprime\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eindex\u003c/code\u003e, and \u003ccode\u003ekind\u003c/code\u003e (see \u003ca href=\"#solving\"\u003eSolving\u003c/a\u003e).\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eRuneSolver.py\u003c/code\u003e contains a specific implementation for each cipher type. Two implementations in particular, \u003ccode\u003eVigenereSolver\u003c/code\u003e which has methods for setting and modifying key material as well as automatic key rotation and interrupt skipping. \u003ccode\u003eSequenceSolver\u003c/code\u003e interprets the cipher on a continuous or discrete function (i.e., Euler's totient).\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eIOWriter.py\u003c/code\u003e handles data ouput to stdout. It does all the word sum calculations, prime word detection, line sums, and output formatting (including colors). automated OEIS sequence checker. The script tests all 294k sequences that contain at least 14 numbers but limits each sequence to the first 40 numbers. For each sequence the script will try to shift the runes and see if a useful word is generated. Useful in this case means it appears in a \u003ca href=\"https://github.com/dwyl/english-words/\"\u003edictionary of 350k words\u003c/a\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eIf all, or all but one, words appear in said dictionary, the seqeuence is printed out. Additionally, the script will also try to shift the generated sequence by all rune indices mod 29. Further, each sequence is tested not only starting at position 0, but also with an offset of -1 to +3 (e.g., 00123 to 345...). Each input is tested with all interrupt combinations (assuming ᚠ is interrupt).\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eAssumptions:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003ethe sequence starts at the beginning\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003ethe beginning is at the top-left and text goes left-to-right\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003ewhitespace is actually correct\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eᚠ is interrupt (or none at all)\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch2 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eHeuristics\u003c/h2\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-heuristics\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Heuristics\" href=\"#heuristics\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThis is where the magic happens. \u003ccode\u003eProbability.py\u003c/code\u003e contains the basic frequency analysis metrics like Index of Coincidence (IoC) and similarity matching. The latter is used to automatically detect key shifts – like in Vigenere or Affine. These metrics are based on english sample texts, in this case “Peace and War” or “Gadsby” (text without the letter ‘e’ [well almost, because there are still 6 e's in there ... liar!]).\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eNGrams.py\u003c/code\u003e is respobsible for taking english text (or any other language) and translating it to runes. Also, counts runes in a text and creates the frequency distribution. The translation is the slowest part, but still very efficient. Creating all 1-gram to 5-grams of a 7 Mb text file takes approx. 20 sec.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eFailedAttempts.py\u003c/code\u003e is a collection of what the title is saying – failed attempts. Currently only holds a n-gram shifter. Which will shift every n runes in contrast to the normal decrypting of a single rune at a time.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch4 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eGuessVigenere, GuessAffine, GuessPattern\u003c/h4\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-guessvigenere-guessaffine-guesspattern\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: GuessVigenere, GuessAffine, GuessPattern\" href=\"#guessvigenere-guessaffine-guesspattern\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThese classes enumerate all possible shifts for a key. For Vigenere that is key length * 29, for Affine key length * 29^2. To determine whether one shift is more likely than another, a similarity metric is used. In this case, the least square distance to a normal english distribution. The value will be lowest if it closely matches the frequencies of each rune.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eGuessPattern\u003c/code\u003e uses an input template, e.g., \u003ccode\u003e1234\u003c/code\u003e and outputs different key permutations such as:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003e1234234134124123\u003c/code\u003e,\u003cbr\u003e\n\u003ccode\u003e1234412334122341\u003c/code\u003e,\u003cbr\u003e\n\u003ccode\u003e1234341212343412\u003c/code\u003e,\u003cbr\u003e\n\u003ccode\u003e12344321\u003c/code\u003e, and \u003ccode\u003e123432\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eInterruptSearch.py\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-interruptsearchpy\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: InterruptSearch.py\" href=\"#interruptsearchpy\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThis is the heart of the interrupt detector. Searching the full set of possible constellations is not feasable (2 ^ {number of possible interrupts}). Thus, the class has two methods to avoid the full search. Both come with a maximum look ahead parameter that can be tweaked.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eLets look at an example with 66 interrupts (p8–14).\u003cbr\u003e\nTesting all would require 2^66 or \u003cstrong\u003e7.4*10^19\u003c/strong\u003e calculations.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch4 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThis will go through the text sequentially. Looking at the first N interrupts and try all combinations in this subset. The best combination will determine whether the current interrupt (1. interrupt index) should be added to the final result. If the current index was used to generate the best value then it is included otherwise not. \u003cstrong\u003eNote:\u003c/strong\u003e it will only add the first interrupt, not all of them. The next iteration will look at the interrupts at index 1 to N+1. Adding the next index if it was in the set, and repeating with the remaining text.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eWith a look ahead of 9 (default value), we have to do (66-8)*2^9 calculations, or \u003cstrong\u003e3.0*10^4\u003c/strong\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch4 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eSearchInterrupt.genetic\u003c/h4\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-searchinterruptgenetic\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: SearchInterrupt.genetic\" href=\"#searchinterruptgenetic\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe genetic approach will look at all interrupts, but only change up to N interrupts at a time. If the look ahead is 4, the algorithm will look at all possible combinations with that will change (up to) 4 interrupts. The best combination is selected and the algorithm repeats. If no better solution is found, the currently best interrupt-set will be returned.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eAs an optimization, smaller look ahead levels are tried first. E.g., if you specify a look ahead of 4, levels 1, 2, and 3 are tried first. The level tells you how many interrupts will be tried simultaniously. Interrupts are like bits and can be flipped either on or off, even multiple times, in a search.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe complexity is not linear and depends on whether “there was just another better solution”. With the default look ahead of 3, which can flip 3 bits simultaneously, each step performs 66!/(3!(66-3)!) + 66!/(2!(66-2)!) + 66 operations or \u003cstrong\u003e4.8*10^4\u003c/strong\u003e. Usually it takes no more than 2–3 steps.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eInterruptDB.py\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-interruptdbpy\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: InterruptDB.py\" href=\"#interruptdbpy\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eCalculating the best interrupt position takes quite long, so we can optimize our program by pre-calculating the IoC's. That is what \u003ccode\u003eInterruptDB.py\u003c/code\u003e is for. The class will search for the best interrupts and store the IoC score as well as the set of interrupts in a file. Later queries just need to process this file instead.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe current configuration will look at the first 20 interrupts, for all runes, on all pages, and up to a key length of 32 – thats 1.36*10^10 operations! The full execution time is somewhere around 38 hours. Luckily, it is a one-time job. <div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Main components:</h3><a id="user-content-main-components" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Main components:" href="#main-components"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>
<p dir="auto"><code>playground.py</code> this is where you want to start. Simply run it and it will greet you with all the posibilities. Use this if you want to experiment, translate runes, check for primes, etc. See <a href="#playground">Playground</a> for more info.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p dir="auto"><code>solver.py</code> you can run <code>solver.py -s</code> to output all already solved pages. Other than that, this is the playground to test new ideas against the unsolved pages. Here you can automate stuff and test it on all the remaining pages; e.g., there is a section to try out totient functions. See <a href="#solving">Solving</a> for more info.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p dir="auto"><code>probability.py</code> some tools for rune frequency analysis, interrupt detector, and Vigenere / Affine breaker. These tools will try to guess the key length of the cipher and determine the most probable key shift per key group. See <a href="#heuristics">Heuristics</a> for more info.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">You can call <code>playground.py</code> and <code>solver.py</code> with command line arguments <code>-v</code> or <code>-q</code> (or both), to control the verbosity of the output (see <a href="#l-log-levels">Log levels</a>).</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">LP pages and notation</h3><a id="user-content-lp-pages-and-notation" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: LP pages and notation" href="#lp-pages-and-notation"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">The <code>pages</code> folder contains all LP pages in text and graphic. Note, I have double checked each and every rune while copying and added missing whitespace characters like <code>'</code> and <code>"</code>.</p>
<p dir="auto">Rune values are taken from Gematria, with these unicode characters representing: space (<code>•</code>), period (<code>⁘</code>), comma (<code>⁚</code>), semicolon (<code>⁖</code>), and chapter mark (<code>⁜</code>).</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">The LP library</h3><a id="user-content-the-lp-library" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: The LP library" href="#the-lp-library"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">These files you probably wont need to touch unless you want to modify some output behavior or rune handling. E.g. if you want to add a rune multiply method. These are the building blocks for the main components.</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>
<p dir="auto"><code>utils.py</code>, a small collection of reusable functions like <code>rev</code>, <code>is_prime</code>, and <code>is_emirp</code> (reverse prime) checking.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p dir="auto"><code>RuneText.py</code> is the representation layer. The class <code>RuneText</code> holds an array of <code>Rune</code> objects, which represent the individual runes. Each <code>Rune</code> has the attributes <code>rune</code>, <code>text</code>, <code>prime</code>, <code>index</code>, and <code>kind</code> (see <a href="#solving">Solving</a>).</p>
</li>
<li>
<p dir="auto"><code>RuneSolver.py</code> contains a specific implementation for each cipher type. Two implementations in particular, <code>VigenereSolver</code> which has methods for setting and modifying key material as well as automatic key rotation and interrupt skipping. <code>SequenceSolver</code> interprets the cipher on a continuous or discrete function (i.e., Euler's totient).</p>
</li>
<li>
<p dir="auto"><code>IOWriter.py</code> handles data ouput to stdout. It does all the word sum calculations, prime word detection, line sums, and output formatting (including colors). Everything you don't want to worry about when processing the actual runes.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p dir="auto">and many more …</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">Refer to <code>solver.py</code> or section <a href="#solving">Solving</a> for examples on usage.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Playground</h2><a id="user-content-playground" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Playground" href="#playground"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">In general, the playground accepts any kind of data. Be it runes, plain text, or comma separated list of indices. So for all commands below you can use whatever<sup>1</sup> you have currently in your clipboard.</p>
<p dir="auto"><sup>1</sup> not primes though, because how would you differentiate an index from a prime?</p>

<p dir="auto">This will search for words of a given length. You may pass either a number (<code>f 7</code>) which will hightlight all 7-rune words or search with a given word. In the latter case it will also provide the substitution for that word, e.g., <code>f pilgrim</code>.</p>

<p dir="auto">Highlighting is currently very limited. The only supported option is <code>hj</code> which will hightlight all interrupts. That is, it will hightlight all occurrences of <code>ᚠ</code> in the text and mark those that are actively skipped or jumped over.<br>
Or use <code>hj x</code> to highlight a different rune (where x is either a number or text).</p>

<p dir="auto">The key length is the sum of user-set-key + offset + padding. Shift and rotate only affect the user set key, not the padding or offset.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Note:</strong> Index 29 is used as placeholder here. A value of 29 will not affect the decryption calculation whatsoever. If a (vigenere) key is set, they key will be split into an active part (values != 29) and an inactive part (values == 29). The output will mark all active runes in red<sup>2</sup>.</p>
<p dir="auto"><sup>2</sup> Totient functions currently do not support highlighting because there is no part that is "not active".</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h4 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Key interrupts / key jumps</h4><a id="user-content-key-interrupts--key-jumps" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Key interrupts / key jumps" href="#key-interrupts--key-jumps"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Some solutions require you to ignore specific <code>ᚠ</code> in the clear text. For example, the solution to jpg 107–167 skips the F rune at position 49 and 58 (ignoring whitespace). You can set these from within the playground.</p>
<p dir="auto">To make things easier, you don't have to use the exact position. Simply used the nth-occurrence of the interrupt. E.g., in the above example you can set the interrupts with <code>kj 2,3</code> (the first occurrence would be index 1).</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">l) Log levels</h3><a id="user-content-l-log-levels" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: l) Log levels" href="#l-log-levels"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Liber Prayground currently supports two log levels. Verbose (<code>lv</code> or <code>-v</code> as CLI args), which will add the prime values of each rune and the sum for each word. And log level Quiet (<code>lq</code> or <code>-q</code> via CLI), which will hide the runes from the ouput. You can combine both.</p>

<p dir="auto">Words which sum up to a prime will be marked. Depending on the log mode the word sum is marked with an asterisk (<code>*</code>) in verbose, or a double underscore (<code>__</code>) in normal mode after the word. In both cases a total sum of the sentence is shown at the end. If that sentence sum is equal to a prime it is marked with an asterisk as well. And if the reverse number is also a prime (emirp) then the sentence is additionally marked with a root square sign (<code>√</code>); in the example above 293 is a prime.</p>

<p dir="auto">As described in <a href="#l-log-levels">log levels</a>, if the number inside prime() is prime it will display a <code>*</code> and/or <code>√</code>. The number inside runes() and plain() is just the length of the string.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">x) Execute decryption and load data</h3><a id="user-content-x-execute-decryption-and-load-data" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: x) Execute decryption and load data" href="#x-execute-decryption-and-load-data"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Running <code>x</code> on its own will decrypt and display the currently loaded data. You can manually set the data by running <code>x Hello world</code>. There is also <code>xf</code> which will load the content of the <code>_input.txt</code> file – or a specific book chapter if you provide it (<code>x p3-7</code>).</p>
<p dir="auto">If the output is too long, you can limit (the already loaded data) with <code>xl 180</code>. Where 180 is the number of characters to display. If the loaded data is a file, you can increase the limit again (or remove it with <code>xl</code>). If the loaded data is manually set, the data is lost forever.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Solving</h2><a id="user-content-solving" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Solving" href="#solving"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Rune and RuneText</h3><a id="user-content-rune-and-runetext" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Rune and RuneText" href="#rune-and-runetext"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto"><code>Rune.kind</code> can be one of <code>r n s l w</code> – meaning (r)une, (n)umber, (s)entence, (l)ine, or (w)hitespace. A line is what you see in the source file (which is equivalent to a line in the original jpg page). A sentence is one that ends with a period (<code>⁘</code>).</p>
<p dir="auto"><code>Rune</code> as well as <code>RuneText</code> both support simple arithmetic operations: <code>Rune(i=2) - 2</code> will yield a <code>ᚠ</code> rune. You can invert text with <code>~RuneText('inverted')</code>.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Note:</strong> Always initialize a rune with its rune character or its index, never ASCII or its prime value.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">RuneTextFile, IOWriter, and I/O</h3><a id="user-content-runetextfile-iowriter-and-io" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: RuneTextFile, IOWriter, and I/O" href="#runetextfile-iowriter-and-io"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Here is a fully working example to load rune data from file, solve it with a vigenere solver, and output it with color highlighting.</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-python notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto"><pre><span class="pl-s1">solver</span> <span class="pl-c1">=</span> <span class="pl-c1">LP</span>.<span class="pl-c1">VigenereSolver</span>()
<span class="pl-s1">solver</span>.<span class="pl-c1">KEY_DATA</span> <span class="pl-c1">=</span> <span class="pl-c1">LP</span>.<span class="pl-c1">RuneText</span>(<span class="pl-s">'divinity'</span>).<span class="pl-c1">index_no_white</span>
<span class="pl-s1">solver</span>.<span class="pl-c1">INTERRUPT_POS</span> <span class="pl-c1">=</span> [<span class="pl-c1">4</span>, <span class="pl-c1">5</span>, <span class="pl-c1">6</span>, <span class="pl-c1">7</span>, <span class="pl-c1">10</span>, <span class="pl-c1">11</span>, <span class="pl-c1">14</span>, <span class="pl-c1">18</span>, <span class="pl-c1">20</span>, <span class="pl-c1">21</span>, <span class="pl-c1">25</span>]
<span class="pl-s1">d_in</span> <span class="pl-c1">=</span> <span class="pl-c1">LP</span>.<span class="pl-c1">RuneTextFile</span>(<span class="pl-c1">LP</span>.<span class="pl-c1">path</span>.<span class="pl-c1">page</span>(<span class="pl-s">'0_welcome'</span>))
<span class="pl-s1">d_out</span>, <span class="pl-s1">_</span> <span class="pl-c1">=</span> <span class="pl-s1">solver</span>.<span class="pl-c1">run</span>(<span class="pl-s1">d_in</span>)
<span class="pl-c1">LP</span>.<span class="pl-c1">IOWriter</span>().<span class="pl-c1">run</span>(<span class="pl-s1">d_out</span>, [(<span class="pl-c1">0</span>, <span class="pl-c1">8</span>), (<span class="pl-c1">510</span>, <span class="pl-c1">517</span>), (<span class="pl-c1">630</span>, <span class="pl-c1">667</span>)])</pre><div class="zeroclipboard-container">
    <clipboard-copy aria-label="Copy code to clipboard" class="ClipboardButton btn btn-invisible js-clipboard-copy m-2 p-0 d-flex flex-justify-center flex-items-center" data-copy-feedback="Copied!" data-tooltip-direction="w" value="solver = LP.VigenereSolver()
solver.KEY_DATA = LP.RuneText('divinity').index_no_white
solver.INTERRUPT_POS = [4, 5, 6, 7, 10, 11, 14, 18, 20, 21, 25]
d_in = LP.RuneTextFile(LP.path.page('0_welcome'))

<p dir="auto">The output writer has the options <code>COLORS</code>, <code>VERBOSE</code>, <code>QUIET</code>, and <code>BREAK_MODE</code> to control the appearance. <code>BREAK_MODE</code> can be one of the <code>Rune.kind</code> values.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">RuneSolver, VigenereSolver, SequenceSolver, AffineSolver, AutokeySolver</h3><a id="user-content-runesolver-vigeneresolver-sequencesolver-affinesolver-autokeysolver" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: RuneSolver, VigenereSolver, SequenceSolver, AffineSolver, AutokeySolver" href="#runesolver-vigeneresolver-sequencesolver-affinesolver-autokeysolver"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">All solver subclasses inherit the attributes of <code>RuneSolver </code> and will include additional data fields that can be set. The most basic form has the two fields <code>INTERRUPT</code> (must be rune) and <code>INTERRUPT_POS</code> (list of indices).</p>
<p dir="auto">In the case of <code>VigenereSolver</code> the additional fields are <code>KEY_DATA</code> (list of indices), <code>KEY_SHIFT</code> (int), <code>KEY_ROTATE</code> (int), <code>KEY_OFFSET</code> (int), and <code>KEY_POST_PAD</code> (int).</p>
<p dir="auto">The class <code>SequenceSolver</code> has only one additional parameter which is <code>FN</code> (function pointer or lambda expression).</p>
<p dir="auto"><code>AffineSolver</code> is very similar to <code>VigenereSolver</code> but uses <code>(a, b)</code> tuples as key data.</p>
<p dir="auto"><code>AutokeySolver</code> is also based on <code>VigenereSolver</code> but reuses key data that was previously decrypted.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">OEIS checker</h3><a id="user-content-oeis-checker" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: OEIS checker" href="#oeis-checker"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto"><code>solver.py</code> has also a fully automated OEIS sequence checker. The script tests all 294k sequences that contain at least 14 numbers but limits each sequence to the first 40 numbers. For each sequence the script will try to shift the runes and see if a useful word is generated. Useful in this case means it appears in a <a href="https://github.com/dwyl/english-words/">dictionary of 350k words</a>.</p>
<p dir="auto">If all, or all but one, words appear in said dictionary, the seqeuence is printed out. Additionally, the script will also try to shift the generated sequence by all rune indices mod 29. Further, each sequence is tested not only starting at position 0, but also with an offset of -1 to +3 (e.g., 00123 to 345...). Each input is tested with all interrupt combinations (assuming ᚠ is interrupt).</p>
<p dir="auto">Assumptions:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>the sequence starts at the beginning</li>
<li>the beginning is at the top-left and text goes left-to-right</li>
<li>whitespace is actually correct</li>
<li>ᚠ is interrupt (or none at all)</li>
</ul>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Heuristics</h2><a id="user-content-heuristics" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Heuristics" href="#heuristics"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">This is where the magic happens. <code>Probability.py</code> contains the basic frequency analysis metrics like Index of Coincidence (IoC) and similarity matching. The latter is used to automatically detect key shifts – like in Vigenere or Affine. These metrics are based on english sample texts, in this case “Peace and War” or “Gadsby” (text without the letter ‘e’ [well almost, because there are still 6 e's in there ... liar!]).</p>
<p dir="auto"><code>NGrams.py</code> is respobsible for taking english text (or any other language) and translating it to runes. Also, counts runes in a text and creates the frequency distribution. The translation is the slowest part, but still very efficient. Creating all 1-gram to 5-grams of a 7 Mb text file takes approx. 20 sec.</p>
<p dir="auto"><code>FailedAttempts.py</code> is a collection of what the title is saying – failed attempts. Currently only holds a n-gram shifter. Which will shift every n runes in contrast to the normal decrypting of a single rune at a time.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h4 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">GuessVigenere, GuessAffine, GuessPattern</h4><a id="user-content-guessvigenere-guessaffine-guesspattern" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: GuessVigenere, GuessAffine, GuessPattern" href="#guessvigenere-guessaffine-guesspattern"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">These classes enumerate all possible shifts for a key. For Vigenere that is key length * 29, for Affine key length * 29^2. To determine whether one shift is more likely than another, a similarity metric is used. In this case, the least square distance to a normal english distribution. The value will be lowest if it closely matches the frequencies of each rune.</p>
<p dir="auto"><code>GuessPattern</code> uses an input template, e.g., <code>1234</code> and outputs different key permutations such as:</p>
<p dir="auto"><code>1234234134124123</code>,<br>
<code>1234412334122341</code>,<br>
<code>1234341212343412</code>,<br>
<code>12344321</code>, and <code>123432</code>.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">InterruptSearch.py</h3><a id="user-content-interruptsearchpy" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: InterruptSearch.py" href="#interruptsearchpy"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">This is the heart of the interrupt detector. Searching the full set of possible constellations is not feasable (2 ^ {number of possible interrupts}). Thus, the class has two methods to avoid the full search. Both come with a maximum look ahead parameter that can be tweaked.</p>
<p dir="auto">Lets look at an example with 66 interrupts (p8–14).<br>
Testing all would require 2^66 or <strong>7.4*10^19</strong> calculations.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h4 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">SearchInterrupt.all</h4><a id="user-content-searchinterruptall" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: SearchInterrupt.all" href="#searchinterruptall"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Just tries all combinations without leaving anything out.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h4 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">SearchInterrupt.sequential</h4><a id="user-content-searchinterruptsequential" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: SearchInterrupt.sequential" href="#searchinterruptsequential"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">This will go through the text sequentially. Looking at the first N interrupts and try all combinations in this subset. The best combination will determine whether the current interrupt (1. interrupt index) should be added to the final result. If the current index was used to generate the best value then it is included otherwise not. <strong>Note:</strong> it will only add the first interrupt, not all of them. The next iteration will look at the interrupts at index 1 to N+1. Adding the next index if it was in the set, and repeating with the remaining text.</p>
<p dir="auto">With a look ahead of 9 (default value), we have to do (66-8)*2^9 calculations, or <strong>3.0*10^4</strong>.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h4 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">SearchInterrupt.genetic</h4><a id="user-content-searchinterruptgenetic" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: SearchInterrupt.genetic" href="#searchinterruptgenetic"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">The genetic approach will look at all interrupts, but only change up to N interrupts at a time. If the look ahead is 4, the algorithm will look at all possible combinations with that will change (up to) 4 interrupts. The best combination is selected and the algorithm repeats. If no better solution is found, the currently best interrupt-set will be returned.</p>
<p dir="auto">As an optimization, smaller look ahead levels are tried first. E.g., if you specify a look ahead of 4, levels 1, 2, and 3 are tried first. The level tells you how many interrupts will be tried simultaniously. Interrupts are like bits and can be flipped either on or off, even multiple times, in a search.</p>
<p dir="auto">The complexity is not linear and depends on whether “there was just another better solution”. With the default look ahead of 3, which can flip 3 bits simultaneously, each step performs 66!/(3!(66-3)!) + 66!/(2!(66-2)!) + 66 operations or <strong>4.8*10^4</strong>. Usually it takes no more than 2–3 steps.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">InterruptDB.py</h3><a id="user-content-interruptdbpy" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: InterruptDB.py" href="#interruptdbpy"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Calculating the best interrupt position takes quite long, so we can optimize our program by pre-calculating the IoC's. That is what <code>InterruptDB.py</code> is for. The class will search for the best interrupts and store the IoC score as well as the set of interrupts in a file. Later queries just need to process this file instead.</p>
<p dir="auto">The current configuration will look at the first 20 interrupts, for all runes, on all pages, and up to a key length of 32 – thats 1.36*10^10 operations! The full execution time is somewhere around 38 hours. Luckily, it is a one-time job. The resulting database is used directly as is, plus a html file is generated by <code>InterruptToWeb.py</code> for a graphical representation. Meanwhile, <code>InterruptIndices.py</code> keeps count how reliable the results are, e.g., how many runes were considered when looking for the first 20 interrupts, and adds that information to the html. Here is the <a href="/relikd/LiberPrayground/blob/main/results">html overview</a>.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">probability.py</h3><a id="user-content-probabilitypy" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: probability.py" href="#probabilitypy"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">As described in the introduction to this repository, <code>probability.py</code> is the third main entry to deciphering the Liber Primus. This includes a fully automated Affine (incl. Atbash, reverse Gematria, xor) and Vigenere breaker.</p>
<p dir="auto">This is your playground to experiment with new automated decrypting and re-running previous tests on new interrupts. Contrary to <code>playground.py</code> (translation, search, key manipulation) and <code>solver.py</code> (automated testing of a specific idea or totient function), <code>probability.py</code> is about automated testing of ideas regarding heuristic metrics. E.g., how can you optimize the process so the program will drop the right answer automatically.</p>
